title: The "Strawman", Magna Carta, Common Law, and More!
summary: Two UK barristers debunk meter-removal advice, the strawman, common law versus statute, maritime law and Magna Carta myths.

assertions.quote: putting in another meter does not mean the electricity or the gas is free it just isn't

verdicts.note: Meter tampering is abstracting electricity, a crime, and the supply charges remain owed.

assertions.quote: straw man isn't defined anywhere in legislation or case law
it's not as though you can just choose whether they apply to you or not

verdicts.note: The argument that failing to provide a license is not a common-law crime and that natural rights were violated was rejected as 'wholly invalid'; the statutory convictions stood.
Claims to be subject only to a romanticized 'common law' (e.g. a guru's tax case) were unsuccessful; the author calls it a mutant version of common law rejected by courts.

All but three provisions of Magna Carta were repealed by 1969, and the High Court of Australia held in 1905 that invalidity for nonconformity with Magna Carta is 'not one for serious refutation'; McHugh J called it political ideals that do not bind parliaments.

The Supreme Court of Canada refused leave to clearly argued claims that Magna Carta, historical common law, the King James Bible or treaties override Canadian law, which the authors read as implicit rejection.

assertions.quote: maritime law in summary is is actually just just really about ships and law of the sea

verdicts.note: Admiralty jurisdiction covers ships, cargo and navigable waters, not traffic, tax or criminal cases against individuals.

A claim that a state family court sat in admiralty and war jurisdiction was dismissed, with cited cases rejecting the same argument about federal and state courts; jurisdiction comes from law, not courtroom symbols.

verdicts.note: The 'win' Menard cited was a New Zealand jury acquittal under a statutory claim-of-right defence with no precedential weight; the protesters were then held liable for $1.2 million and the defence was abolished.

A few charged tax protesters avoided conviction but the vast majority are convicted; Cheek's reversal was on jury instructions about willfulness, not on the theory, and he was convicted on remand; acquittal does not bar civil liability.
The guru acquittals cited were on ordinary grounds: Porisky because the Crown had not proved its non-filing records, Naudi because the Crown had not linked him to his SIN.

The cited exceptions are procedural: a conviction was overturned because the judge ruled after letting a flesh-and-blood defendant leave, and a NZ judge found an ordinary contract claim inside sovereign pleadings.

assertions.quote: freedom online is just a way of arguing a parking fine into a jail sentence
self-represented people literally in person are bound by all the same rules and requirements as legal professionals

verdicts.note: UK courts (Barton v Wright Hassall) and US courts give litigants in person little procedural leeway beyond liberal reading of pleadings.
The court warned the pro se defendant, with appellate approval, that he would be held to the same rules of evidence and procedure as if represented by an attorney.
Pro se pleadings are held to 'less stringent standards' than lawyers' drafts, but a pro se plaintiff is not excused from basic jurisdictional requirements: lenient reading, same core rules.
In Canada, Pintea v Johns endorsed principles rejecting identical rules of evidence and procedure for self-represented and represented litigants; true in some systems, not others.
In Pintea v Johns the SCC called SRLs a special category needing different treatment because they know less law and procedure; OPCA litigants are still treated as abusive.

assertions.quote: there are only four clauses of magna carta still still really of any relevance today

verdicts.note: By 1969 the whole Charter, save three provisions, had been repealed in England.
